messages:
maria: Heads up — prod gpu-12 hit an OOM twice in ~3h window for long-context jobs after yesterday's batching heuristic tweak. Logs point to the prefix pool blowing up, not model mem.

maria: error excerpt:
```
[2026-03-18T13:02:14Z] runtime: KV cache OOM allocating 32768 pages for prefix pool (requested 256MB)
stack: runtime/alloc -> prefix_pool::reserve -> kv_cache::insert_prefix
```

ajay: I repro on staging with longconv-50k test. pprof shows steady growth in prefix_pool arenas and very low reuse counts. Slab fragmentation ~42%.

ajay: pprof top:
```
Total: 1.2GB
  480MB 40.0%  prefix_pool::alloc_prefix
  250MB 20.8%  kernel_selection::choose_kernel (new path)
  200MB 16.6%  batching::window_alloc
```

will: quick heap check: biggest live objects are tokenized-prefix entries (avg 6k per prefix). Reuse metric is low — evicted prefixes aren't being reused so eviction doesn't reclaim contiguous pages.

zoe: Immediate mitigations we can flip now (low risk):
- set `max_prefix_reserve` down to `64MB`
- enable `kv_soft_evict=true` (prefer compaction-friendly eviction)
- throttle `max_context_tokens` to `32k` for hosted tier
Also propose a rollback of the batching heuristic change (commit 9c7f2bd) if flags don't help.

henry: We should also add an emergency routing fallback: requests with context > 48k -> `redwood-mini-1` (stateless small-model) so we avoid heavy KV pressure. Can implement as a routing policy override.

sre-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created INC-2026-045. On-call notified.

carol: Plan:
1) Apply soft_eviction + lower max_prefix_reserve to 64MB on a 10% canary ring now.
2) Watch metrics for 30m: `kv_free_rate`, `slab_frag_ratio`, `page_faults/sec`, `oom_count`, `avg_batch_window_ms`.
3) If no improvement, rollback batching commit and route >48k to fallback model.
I can run the flag toggle at 14:15 UTC.

maria: Doing step 1 on gpu-12 canary now. `kv_soft_evict=true` and `max_prefix_reserve=64MB` applied to canary hosts. Monitoring. :eyes: :pray:

ajay: Note from repro: increasing batch window from 5ms -> 20ms increased in-flight requests by ~3x for long-context flows; combined with kernel-selection picking the FP16 kernel, the prefix pool allocation pattern changed (more small allocations scattered across slabs) which boosted fragmentation. Suspect two-factor interaction.

will: Temporary toggle command I used (ops/admin API):
```bash
curl -XPOST https://ops-api.internal/flags \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPSTOKEN' \\n  -d '{"kv_soft_evict": true, "max_prefix_reserve": "64MB"}'
```

maria: After 12m on canary: kv_free_rate up 2x, slab_frag_ratio down 6 pts, no OOMs so far. Keeping canary for another 20m then rolling to 50% if stable.

carol: If we see regression after scaling flags, rollback path is ready: `git revert 9c7f2bd` + quick deploy of previous kernel-selection binary. I'll coordinate.

henry: Follow-up items (postmortem):
- add a regression test that runs long-context synthetic load against batching-window variants
- instrument `prefix_reuse_ratio` in runtime telemetry
- consider defragmenting compaction in background for prefix pool
- add a soft-fallback route at router level for >48k contexts

maria: Good notes. Thanks everyone — will update incident ticket with timeline and metrics graphs.
